name: PT-141 / Bremelanotide
title: Central melanocortin signaling
mechanism: Bremelanotide is a melanocortin receptor agonist. MC1R and MC4R binding occur at therapeutic exposures; the precise mechanism of benefit in HSDD remains unknown. MC4R-related pathways are a biological rationale, not a complete explanation of an individual response. Avoid presenting a single “libido switch”. RECONNECT used FSFI desire and FSDS-DAO item 13 as coprimary outcomes in premenopausal women with HSDD. Two 24-week randomized trials supported the defined indication. The label reports no significant treatment difference in the number of satisfying sexual events.
scope: The pivotal evidence and US label concern a specified subcutaneous bremelanotide product. A compounded pen or nasal spray is not automatically equivalent.

scope: The foundational treatment experiments used administered peptide in animals. Human exercise studies measured endogenous MOTS-c. Those are different exposures from a compounded subcutaneous pen.

name: RU58841
title: Androgen-receptor research
mechanism: RU58841 antagonizes androgen-receptor activation in experimental systems. The response depends on tissue and hormone context. Preclinical growth does not establish long-term human benefit or safety.
scope: A topical experimental solution is not a validated commercial treatment.

name: Testosterone / TRT

mechanism: Formulation influences exposure and monitoring. Receptor-mediated effects depend on baseline state and endpoint. LH/FSH and sperm production can be suppressed; fertility goals matter.
scope: Match the licensed formulation and clinical monitoring context.
